Absent predicate execution is a W-boundary matter, not a defeater of this established semantic gap.

contracts.quote: transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal
contracts.reason: NL1 establishes an explicit transition from DoorsClosing to InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of both alternatives.
Stopping is one alternative destination.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to Stopping.
contracts.quote: can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal
contracts.reason: NL2 presents Stopping as one alternative target from InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of both alternatives.
EmergencyStopping is the other alternative destination.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to EmergencyStopping.
contracts.quote: or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL2 presents EmergencyStopping as the second alternative target from InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: Shared source of the two alternatives.

contracts.normative_statement: The Stopping and EmergencyStopping alternatives from InMotion must be distinguishable/mutually exclusive.
contracts.quote: either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives ... or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL2 uses 'either...or' explicitly presenting two mutually exclusive alternative conditions (arrival vs obstacle detection) from the same source.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the origin state from which EmergencyStopping is entered per NL2/NL3 discourse.

contracts.normative_statement: The system must enter EmergencyStopping when an obstacle is detected.

binding_hints.reason: EmergencyStopping is the owner of this effect.

contracts.reason: NL3 independently requires the sending of the Obstacle Detected signal as a separate effect from the Emergency Stop action.

Key finding: FCSTM's InMotion internal transitions route to InMotion's own pseudo-exit ([*] with effect setting R45RouteToken) which is then dispatched by outer InMotion->Stopping/EmergencyStopping/InMotion(self) transitions guarded on R45RouteToken. The Stopping state is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF), which is expected since Stopping is presumably a terminal state in NL, but NL never explicitly declares Stopping as a termination_state requiring further continuation, so this is not flagged as a termination contract violation absent an explicit termination contract. All seven event-consumer facts show declared consumers equal to reachable consumers, so NL2-DERIVED, NL1-DERIVED, NL5-DERIVED, NL6-DERIVED, NL7-DERIVED, and NL2-DERIVED(arrival) event-consumption contracts are satisfied and omitted. All named states (DoorsClosing, InMotion, Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching, Stopping, EmergencyStopping) are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts, satisfying root reachability for NL1-INIT-1, NL5-INIT-1 endpoint/entry contracts region. No forbidden-scope entry evident. The InMotion->InMotion self-loop diagnostic (I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT) is informational only and not tied to any supplied contract. No additional derived contracts are warranted since all consumer/reachability facts close positively and Stopping's dead-end is not bound to any explicit termination or deadlock_freedom NL contract (NL2-ENDPOINT-1 merely requires InMotion->Stopping edge existence, which exists through the macro-routed path).

Because the closed model never executes 'Send Obstacle Detected' as an action and instead waits on a literally named compound event, the obligation is violated on these exact facts. The candidate's supplied strongest_rebuttal only asserts self-consistency of the closed model and attributes the gap to the lowering process, without presenting any exact fact establishing that 'Send Obstacle Detected' is executed as an effect elsewhere. Since the exact opaque-event binding directly contradicts this rebuttal and no exact supporting fact exists, the defeater is defeated. The null predicate_id and unsupported/unknown backend verdict reflect only executability limits (a W-boundary matter) and do not bear on this semantic determination.
